wb_co2_per_capita.note: Tonnes of CO2 per capita, excluding land use. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: CO2 Emissions per Person
meta.subtitle: Tonnes of CO2 per capita, excluding land use

explain.what: Carbon dioxide released per Indian each year from fossil fuels, cement and industry.
explain.read: A rising line means emissions are growing faster than population. India's figure is about a third of the world average and a sixth of the US level.
explain.why: Per-person emissions frame India's climate-equity argument: total emissions are large, but each citizen's footprint is small.

wb_total_ghg.note: Million tonnes of CO2-equivalent, excluding land use. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator EN.GHG.ALL.MT.CE.AR5); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Total Greenhouse Gas Emissions
meta.subtitle: Million tonnes of CO2-equivalent, excluding land use

explain.what: All greenhouse gases India emits each year (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide and F-gases), converted to CO2-equivalent.
explain.read: The slope shows how fast emissions are growing; compare it with GDP growth to judge whether the economy is decarbonising.
explain.why: India is now the world's third-largest emitter in total, which makes its 2070 net-zero pathway globally significant.

wb_protected_areas.note: Terrestrial and marine protected areas, % of territory. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator ER.PTD.TOTL.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Protected Areas
meta.subtitle: Terrestrial and marine protected areas, % of territory

explain.what: The share of India's land and territorial waters inside national parks, sanctuaries and other protected areas.
explain.read: Higher is more protected; the global 30x30 target asks countries to protect 30% by 2030.
explain.why: Protected areas safeguard tigers, elephants and watersheds, but expanding them must be balanced against forest-dwellers' rights.

wb_freshwater_per_capita.note: Cubic metres of internal renewable water per person. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator ER.H2O.INTR.PC); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Renewable Freshwater per Person
meta.subtitle: Cubic metres of internal renewable water per person

explain.what: How much renewable freshwater (rivers and groundwater recharge) India has per person.
explain.read: The total resource is roughly fixed, so the line falls as population grows. Below 1,700 m3 a country is 'water-stressed'; below 1,000 it is 'water-scarce'.
explain.why: Falling water per person explains groundwater depletion, inter-State river disputes and the push for micro-irrigation and Jal Jeevan Mission.

wb_population_density.note: People per square kilometre of land. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator EN.POP.DNST); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Population Density
meta.subtitle: People per square kilometre of land

explain.what: The average number of people living on each square kilometre of India's land.
explain.read: A steadily rising line; India is one of the most densely populated large countries.
explain.why: Density raises pressure on land, forests, water and cities, and shapes disaster exposure.

wb_fertiliser_per_ha.note: Kg of N+P+K nutrients per hectare of arable land. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator AG.CON.FERT.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Fertiliser Use per Hectare
meta.subtitle: Kg of N+P+K nutrients per hectare of arable land

explain.what: How intensively Indian farmland is fertilised: kilograms of nitrogen, phosphate and potash applied per hectare.
explain.read: A rising line means more intensive farming. Compare it with cereal yields to see whether extra fertiliser still raises output.
explain.why: Heavy, unbalanced fertiliser use raises the subsidy bill and degrades soil and groundwater, which is why soil-health cards and nano-urea are being promoted.

wb_irrigated_land.note: Share of agricultural land that is irrigated, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator AG.LND.IRIG.AG.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Irrigated Agricultural Land
meta.subtitle: Share of agricultural land that is irrigated, %

explain.what: The share of India's agricultural land that receives irrigation rather than depending only on rain.
explain.read: Higher means farming is better protected from monsoon failures.
explain.why: Irrigation is the biggest buffer against drought; PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana aims to extend it to every farm.

wb_arable_land_per_capita.note: Hectares of arable land per person. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator AG.LND.ARBL.HA.PC); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Arable Land per Person
meta.subtitle: Hectares of arable land per person

explain.what: How much cropland India has for each person.
explain.read: The line falls as population grows on a fixed land base; fragmentation means the average farm holding is now about one hectare.
explain.why: Shrinking land per person makes productivity growth, not area expansion, the only route to feeding more people.

wb_food_production_index.note: Index of food output, 2014-2016 = 100. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator AG.PRD.FOOD.XD); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Food Production Index
meta.subtitle: Index of food output, 2014-2016 = 100

explain.what: A volume index of all food crops and livestock produced in India, set to 100 for 2014-2016.
explain.read: A value of 120 means 20% more food than the 2014-16 average. Steady growth with few dips shows resilient farm output.
explain.why: It summarises whether food supply is keeping pace with population and demand.

wb_undernourishment.note: Share of population below minimum calorie needs, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Prevalence of Undernourishment
meta.subtitle: Share of population below minimum calorie needs, %

explain.what: The FAO estimate of the share of Indians whose usual food intake does not meet minimum energy needs.
explain.read: Lower is better. It is a three-year average, so it moves slowly.
explain.why: Hunger is SDG 2 and the target of the National Food Security Act and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana; this is also an input to the Global Hunger Index.

wb_child_stunting.note: Children under 5 too short for their age, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.STA.STNT.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Child Stunting (modelled)
meta.subtitle: Children under 5 too short for their age, %

explain.what: The share of children under five who are too short for their age, a sign of chronic undernutrition.
explain.read: Lower is better; the trend comes from UNICEF/WHO/World Bank modelled estimates that smooth survey years (NFHS).
explain.why: Stunting harms brain development and lifetime earnings and is the main target of POSHAN Abhiyaan.

wb_measles_immunisation.note: Children aged 12-23 months vaccinated, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.IMM.MEAS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Measles Immunisation
meta.subtitle: Children aged 12-23 months vaccinated, %

explain.what: The share of young children who have received the measles vaccine.
explain.read: Higher is better; at least 95% is needed to stop measles outbreaks. Dips show disruptions such as COVID-19.
explain.why: Measles coverage is a bellwether for the whole routine-immunisation system under Mission Indradhanush.

wb_youth_unemployment.note: Unemployed as % of labour force aged 15-24. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SL.UEM.1524.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Youth Unemployment (ILO estimate)
meta.subtitle: Unemployed as % of labour force aged 15-24

explain.what: The ILO-modelled unemployment rate for young people aged 15-24, comparable across countries.
explain.read: Read it with the PLFS youth chart: the methods differ, but both show youth unemployment far above the overall rate.
explain.why: It shows how well the economy absorbs new entrants into the workforce each year.

wb_women_in_parliament.note: Share of Lok Sabha seats held by women, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SG.GEN.PARL.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Women in Parliament
meta.subtitle: Share of Lok Sabha seats held by women, %

explain.what: The share of seats in the lower house of Parliament held by women.
explain.read: Steps in the line follow general elections. The Women's Reservation Act (2023) will reserve one-third of seats once it takes effect.
explain.why: Representation shapes which issues reach the legislative agenda.

wb_rnd_spending.note: Gross domestic spending on R&D, % of GDP. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Research & Development Spending
meta.subtitle: Gross domestic spending on R&D, % of GDP

explain.what: Total spending on research and development by government, business and universities as a share of GDP.
explain.read: India's figure stays near 0.7%, against about 2.5% in China and over 3% in the US and South Korea.
explain.why: R&D drives innovation and productivity; the Anusandhan National Research Foundation is meant to lift private research spending.

wb_researchers.note: Full-time researchers in R&D per million population. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SP.POP.SCIE.RD.P6); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: Researchers per Million People
meta.subtitle: Full-time researchers in R&D per million population

explain.what: The number of people working full-time in research per million population.
explain.read: Higher means a larger research workforce; India's figure is low by international standards.
explain.why: A country's research base decides its ability to innovate in fields from vaccines to semiconductors.

wb_ict_service_exports.note: Computer, communications and other services, % of service exports. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

meta.title: ICT Service Exports
meta.subtitle: Computer, communications and other services, % of service exports

explain.what: The share of India's service exports that come from IT, software, communications and related business services.
explain.read: A high, rising share shows how central the IT and global-capability-centre industry is to India's exports.
explain.why: Services exports pay for much of India's merchandise trade deficit, making this sector a pillar of external stability.

meta.title: All-India Mean Temperature by Season
meta.subtitle: Area-weighted average temperature, °C (IMD)

explain.what: The India Meteorological Department's all-India average air temperature for the whole year and for each season, from 2001.
explain.read: Each line is one season. A line that drifts upward over the years means that season is getting warmer; compare the annual line with the pre-monsoon line to see where heat is concentrated.
explain.why: Rising temperatures drive heat stress, crop losses, power demand and water scarcity, so this is the baseline for every climate-adaptation discussion.

mospi_mean_temperature.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 1 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: All-India Annual Rainfall
meta.subtitle: Sum of monthly all-India rainfall, mm (IMD)

explain.what: Total rainfall received across India in each calendar year, built by adding the IMD's twelve monthly all-India averages.
explain.read: Taller bars are wetter years. Look for short bars: they usually line up with drought years and weak monsoons, such as 2002, 2009 and 2014-15.
explain.why: Roughly half of India's farmland is rain-fed, so a poor rainfall year shows up quickly in farm output, rural incomes, food prices and reservoir levels.

mospi_annual_rainfall.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Southwest Monsoon Rainfall (June-September)
meta.subtitle: Sum of June-September all-India rainfall, mm (IMD)

explain.what: Rain delivered by the southwest monsoon, the four months from June to September, in each year.
explain.read: Compare each bar with the others: the monsoon normally brings about three-quarters of India's annual rain, so dips here explain most dry years in the annual chart.
explain.why: Kharif sowing, groundwater recharge, hydropower and rural demand all depend on the monsoon; the RBI and the Finance Ministry track it closely for inflation and growth.

mospi_monsoon_rainfall.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Cyclonic Storms over the North Indian Ocean
meta.subtitle: Storms formed in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea per year (IMD)

explain.what: The number of cyclonic storms that formed each year over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea, as recorded by the IMD.
explain.read: Each bar counts storms, not damage. Year-to-year swings are natural; look at decades together to judge whether storms are becoming more frequent.
explain.why: Cyclones threaten a coastline that is home to millions of people. Better forecasting and evacuation have cut deaths sharply even when storm counts have not fallen.

mospi_cyclonic_storms.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 89 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Heat Wave Days by State (2024)
meta.subtitle: Average heat wave days in the summer season (IMD)

explain.what: How many heat wave days each State recorded in the most recent summer season, as declared by the IMD.
explain.read: Longer bars mean more days of dangerous heat. Northern and central plains usually top the list.
explain.why: Heat waves kill outdoor workers, the elderly and the poor, cut labour productivity and stress power grids; State heat-action plans target the worst-hit regions.

mospi_heat_wave_days.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 87 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2024. Ranked highest to lowest.

meta.title: India's Forest Cover
meta.subtitle: Total forest cover, sq km (Forest Survey of India)

explain.what: Total area under forest cover in India from each State of Forest Report, built from satellite mapping by the Forest Survey of India.
explain.read: Each point is one biennial assessment; a rising line means more mapped forest cover. Mapping methods and resolution have improved over time, so small changes are within error.
explain.why: Forests store carbon, protect watersheds and support tribal livelihoods; India's climate pledge includes adding a carbon sink of 2.5-3 billion tonnes through forests and tree cover.

mospi_forest_cover_trend.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 20 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). The source files the national total under a State label in some years; it is detected and used as the all-India value.

meta.title: Forest Cover by State (2023)
meta.subtitle: Forest cover in the latest State of Forest Report, sq km

explain.what: The forest area of each State and UT in the most recent State of Forest Report.
explain.read: Bars are absolute areas, so large States lead. Madhya Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha usually hold the biggest forests.
explain.why: Forest-rich States carry much of India's carbon sink and biodiversity; forest area is also one factor in how the Finance Commission shares central taxes with States.

labels: Daman and Diu and Dadra Nagar Haveli
mospi_forest_cover_states.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 20 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2023. Ranked highest to lowest.

meta.title: Municipal Solid Waste Generated by State (2021-22)
meta.subtitle: Tonnes per day (CPCB)

explain.what: How much municipal solid waste (household and commercial garbage) each State's urban local bodies generate per day, as reported to the Central Pollution Control Board.
explain.read: Longer bars mean more waste each day. Populous, urbanised States such as Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi generate the most.
explain.why: Waste volumes set the scale of collection, processing and landfill capacity cities need under the Solid Waste Management Rules and Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban).

mospi_msw_generation_states.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 80 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2021-22. Ranked highest to lowest. Values are shown as published; Uttarakhand's reported figure is unusually high relative to its population.

meta.title: Urban Waste: Generated, Collected, Treated, Landfilled (2021-22)
meta.subtitle: All-India municipal solid waste, tonnes per day (CPCB)

explain.what: All-India totals of municipal solid waste generated, collected, scientifically treated and sent to landfill each day.
explain.read: Read the bars left to right as a funnel: the gap between Generated and Collected is waste left on streets, and the gap between Collected and Treated is waste dumped without processing.
explain.why: The treated share is the clearest measure of whether cities are actually managing waste rather than just moving it to dumpsites.

mospi_msw_management_funnel.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 80 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2021-22. All-India figures are the sum of State/UT reports for the latest year.

meta.title: Plastic Waste Generated
meta.subtitle: Estimated plastic waste, tonnes per annum (CPCB)

explain.what: Estimated plastic waste generated across India each year, summed from State Pollution Control Board reports to the CPCB.
explain.read: Bars show the national total. Jumps can reflect better reporting by States as well as real growth in plastic use.
explain.why: Plastic waste clogs drains, pollutes rivers and seas and is the target of India's single-use plastic ban and Extended Producer Responsibility rules.

mospi_plastic_waste.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 132 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). National totals are the sum of State/UT estimates.

meta.title: Deaths from Forces of Nature by Cause (2022)
meta.subtitle: Share of accidental deaths due to natural causes (NCRB)

explain.what: How deaths attributed to forces of nature in the latest year split by cause, from NCRB's Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India.
explain.read: Bigger slices are bigger killers. Lightning is usually the largest single cause, ahead of floods and heat stroke.
explain.why: Lightning and heat kill more people than dramatic disasters such as earthquakes, which points disaster-risk spending toward early warnings and shelters.

mospi_nature_deaths_by_cause.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 94 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2022.

meta.title: Deaths from Forces of Nature
meta.subtitle: Total accidental deaths due to natural causes (NCRB)

explain.what: The total number of people killed by natural causes (lightning, floods, heat, cold, landslides, storms and others) each year.
explain.read: Each bar is one year. Spikes usually match a severe flood, cyclone or heat season.
explain.why: This tracks the human cost of climate and weather extremes, and whether early-warning systems are saving lives.

mospi_nature_deaths_trend.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 94 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Electricity Generation by Source (2023-24)
meta.subtitle: Share of gross generation, GWh (CEA)

explain.what: Where India's electricity came from in the latest year, by fuel, from Central Electricity Authority data.
explain.read: Each slice is a share of total generation. Coal still dominates; the renewables slice (solar, wind, small hydro, biomass) is the one to watch.
explain.why: India has pledged 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 and net zero by 2070, so the coal-to-renewables balance is the core energy-transition metric.

mospi_power_generation_mix.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 41 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2023-24.

meta.title: Electricity Generation since Independence
meta.subtitle: Gross generation by source, GWh (CEA)

explain.what: Gross electricity generated in India by source from 1947 to the latest year.
explain.read: Lines show absolute output, so thermal power's steep climb shows how India electrified. Renewables appear only from the 2000s and are now rising fastest.
explain.why: Electricity use tracks industrialisation and living standards; the mix shows how carbon-intensive that growth has been.

mospi_power_generation_trend.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 41 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Foodgrain Production
meta.subtitle: Million tonnes (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare)

explain.what: India's production of rice, wheat, coarse cereals (millets, maize) and pulses, and their total, for each crop year (July-June).
explain.read: The top line is total foodgrains; the lines below show what it is made of. Dips usually follow drought years such as 2009-10 and 2014-15.
explain.why: Foodgrain output underpins food security, the public distribution system (PDS) and food inflation. Pulses matter because India still imports to meet demand.

mospi_foodgrain_production.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 51 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Oilseed Production
meta.subtitle: Lakh tonnes (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare)

explain.what: Production of India's nine major oilseeds and the three biggest of them: soybean, rapeseed-mustard and groundnut.
explain.read: Compare the total with the three crops below it to see which crop is driving growth or decline.
explain.why: India imports more than half of its edible oil, so domestic oilseed output decides the import bill and is the target of the National Mission on Edible Oils.

mospi_oilseed_cash_crops.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 51 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). The API labels these rows 'Million tonnes', but the magnitudes match the Ministry's lakh-tonne series (for example 2023-24 nine oilseeds = 416.7 lakh tonnes).

meta.title: Sugarcane Production
meta.subtitle: Lakh tonnes (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare)

explain.what: Total sugarcane harvested in India in each crop year.
explain.read: Higher values mean a bigger cane crop; the swings follow monsoon rainfall and irrigation in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
explain.why: Sugarcane feeds the sugar industry and the ethanol-blending programme, but it is very water-intensive, which ties it to groundwater depletion debates.

mospi_sugarcane_production.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 51 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). The API labels these rows 'Million tonnes', but the magnitudes match the Ministry's lakh-tonne series (2023-24 = 4,351 lakh tonnes, about 435 million tonnes).

meta.title: Fertiliser Consumption by Nutrient
meta.subtitle: Lakh tonnes of N, P and K (Department of Fertilizers)

explain.what: How much nitrogen, phosphate and potash fertiliser Indian farmers used each year since 1981-82, in nutrient terms.
explain.read: Nitrogen (mostly urea) towers over the others. The agronomic ideal is roughly 4:2:1 for N:P:K, so a widening gap signals unbalanced use.
explain.why: Fertiliser subsidies are one of the largest items in the Union Budget, and overuse of urea degrades soil and water; this chart shows the scale of both.

mospi_fertiliser_consumption.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 54 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Fertiliser: Consumption vs Production vs Imports
meta.subtitle: Total N+P+K, lakh tonnes (Department of Fertilizers)

explain.what: Total fertiliser nutrients consumed in India against what was produced domestically and what was imported.
explain.read: When the consumption line sits above production, the gap is filled by imports. Watch whether new urea plants narrow that gap.
explain.why: Import dependence exposes farmers and the subsidy bill to global gas and fertiliser prices, as in 2022.

mospi_fertiliser_self_reliance.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 54 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Livestock Population by Species
meta.subtitle: Million animals, Livestock Census (DAHD)

explain.what: The number of cattle, buffaloes, goats, sheep and pigs counted in each Livestock Census since 1951.
explain.read: Each point is a census year. Cattle numbers have plateaued while buffaloes and goats have grown, reflecting the shift to dairy and meat.
explain.why: Livestock supports about a fifth of rural households and makes India the world's largest milk producer.

mospi_livestock_census.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 61 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Fish Production: Inland vs Marine
meta.subtitle: Lakh tonnes (Department of Fisheries)

explain.what: Fish produced in India each year from inland waters (rivers, reservoirs and fish farms) and from the sea.
explain.read: Inland production overtook marine catch in the 1990s and now dominates; that is the aquaculture boom.
explain.why: India is the world's second-largest fish producer, and fisheries support millions of coastal and rural livelihoods and a major seafood-export trade.

mospi_fish_production.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 64 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Labour Force Participation Rate (PLFS)
meta.subtitle: Share of people aged 15+ working or seeking work

explain.what: The share of people aged 15 and over who are in the labour force (working or looking for work), from the Periodic Labour Force Survey.
explain.read: Compare the women's line with the men's: the gap shows how many women are outside paid work. A rising women's line is the biggest labour-market change since 2017-18.
explain.why: Participation, not just unemployment, decides how much of India's demographic dividend turns into output and household income.

plfs_lfpr_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 1 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

meta.title: Worker Population Ratio (PLFS)
meta.subtitle: Share of people aged 15+ who are employed

explain.what: The share of the population aged 15 and over that is actually employed.
explain.read: This is the employment rate: it rises when jobs grow faster than population. Read it alongside the participation chart.
explain.why: It is the most direct measure of how many people the economy employs, and it includes self-employment and unpaid family work.

plfs_wpr_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 2 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

meta.title: Unemployment Rate (PLFS)
meta.subtitle: Share of the labour force aged 15+ without work

explain.what: The share of people in the labour force (aged 15+) who looked for work but found none.
explain.read: Lower is better. A falling line together with a rising participation rate is a genuinely tightening labour market.
explain.why: This is India's official headline unemployment measure, used for policy and to compare States.

plfs_unemployment_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

meta.title: Youth Unemployment Rate, 15-29 (PLFS)
meta.subtitle: Share of the labour force aged 15-29 without work

explain.what: The unemployment rate among young people aged 15-29.
explain.read: Youth unemployment runs well above the overall rate; watch the gap between young women and young men.
explain.why: Joblessness among educated young people is a key political and economic issue and the target of skilling and apprenticeship schemes.

plfs_youth_unemployment.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

meta.title: Infant Mortality Rate by Sex (SRS)
meta.subtitle: Deaths before age one per 1,000 live births

explain.what: Out of every 1,000 babies born alive, how many die before their first birthday, from the Registrar General's Sample Registration System.
explain.read: All lines falling means more infants survive. Girls' mortality was once higher than boys', which is unusual biologically; watch whether that gap has closed.
explain.why: Infant mortality is a summary of maternal health, nutrition, immunisation and sanitation; SDG 3 asks India to keep pushing it down.

mospi_imr_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 15 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Under-Five Mortality Rate by Sex (SRS)
meta.subtitle: Deaths before age five per 1,000 live births

explain.what: Deaths of children before their fifth birthday per 1,000 live births, from the Sample Registration System.
explain.read: Lower is better; the SDG target is 25 or fewer by 2030. Compare girls with boys for signs of gender bias in child care.
explain.why: Under-five deaths are mostly preventable (pneumonia, diarrhoea, newborn complications), so this measures how well basic health services reach children.

mospi_u5mr_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 17 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Life Expectancy at Birth by Sex (SRS)
meta.subtitle: Years, five-year moving periods

explain.what: How many years a newborn would live on average if current death rates held, from SRS abridged life tables for overlapping five-year periods.
explain.read: Both lines rising means longer lives. Women overtook men in the 1990s and the gap has widened, the normal pattern as health care improves.
explain.why: Life expectancy sums up a country's health in one number and shapes pension, health and elder-care planning.

mospi_life_expectancy_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 18 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Projected periods (2021-25 onward) published alongside the estimates are excluded.

meta.title: Maternal Mortality Ratio (SRS)
meta.subtitle: Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births

explain.what: Women who die from pregnancy or childbirth complications per 100,000 live births, from SRS special bulletins on maternal mortality.
explain.read: Each bar is a pooled period (for example 2018-20). India has passed its National Health Policy target of 100 and is heading toward the SDG goal of 70.
explain.why: The fall reflects institutional deliveries under Janani Suraksha Yojana and better emergency obstetric care, and shows what is left to do.

mospi_maternal_mortality.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 21 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Maternal Mortality Ratio by State (SRS) (2021-23)
meta.subtitle: Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births

explain.what: The maternal mortality ratio in each larger State for the latest SRS period.
explain.read: Longer bars are worse. Assam, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh usually rank highest; Kerala, Maharashtra and Telangana lowest.
explain.why: The spread between States shows that national progress hides large regional gaps where maternal-health spending is most needed.

mospi_maternal_mortality_states.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 21 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2021-23. Ranked highest to lowest.

meta.title: Sex Ratio at Birth (SRS)
meta.subtitle: Girls born per 1,000 boys, three-year periods

explain.what: How many girls are born for every 1,000 boys, from the Sample Registration System.
explain.read: The natural ratio is about 950. Values well below that point to sex-selective abortion; an upward trend means the gap is closing.
explain.why: This is the key outcome for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and the PC-PNDT Act, and it shapes future marriage markets and demography.

mospi_sex_ratio_at_birth.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 7 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Population Sex Ratio (Census 1951-2011)
meta.subtitle: Females per 1,000 males

explain.what: Females per 1,000 males in the whole population at each Census from 1951 to 2011.
explain.read: A value below 1,000 means fewer women than men. India's ratio dipped to 927 in 1991 and recovered to 943 by 2011.
explain.why: A persistently low sex ratio reflects excess female mortality and son preference; it is one of the starkest gender indicators.

mospi_census_sex_ratio.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 2 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Women's Mean Age at Marriage (SRS)
meta.subtitle: Average age at effective marriage, years

explain.what: The average age at which women marry, from the Sample Registration System.
explain.read: Higher is better for health and education outcomes. Urban women marry about two years later than rural women.
explain.why: Later marriage is linked to more schooling, lower fertility and better maternal and child health; it is also behind the debate on raising the legal age of marriage to 21.

mospi_women_age_at_marriage.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 14 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Total Fertility Rate by Women's Education (SRS) (2023)
meta.subtitle: Children per woman

explain.what: The average number of children a woman would have over her life, grouped by her education level, for the latest SRS year.
explain.read: Bars fall from left to right: illiterate women have the most children and graduates the fewest.
explain.why: Girls' education is one of the most powerful levers on population growth, maternal health and child welfare.

mospi_tfr_by_education.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 10 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2023.

meta.title: Literacy Rate by Sex (age 7+)
meta.subtitle: Census 1981-2011 and NSS 2017-18, %

explain.what: The share of people aged seven and over who can read and write, from the Census and the NSS 75th round (2017-18).
explain.read: The gap between men's and women's lines is the gender literacy gap; it has narrowed steadily since 1981.
explain.why: Literacy is the base for employability, health awareness and civic participation, and women's literacy in particular predicts child health.

mospi_literacy_by_sex.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 55 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Gross Enrolment Ratio by Stage (UDISE+/AISHE)
meta.subtitle: Enrolment as % of the official age group

explain.what: Enrolment at each stage of education as a percentage of the population of the matching age group.
explain.read: Primary is near or above 100% (universal), but each later stage is lower: the drop between lines shows where children leave school.
explain.why: The National Education Policy targets 100% GER up to secondary level and 50% in higher education by 2035.

mospi_school_ger.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 60 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: School Dropout Rate by Stage (UDISE+)
meta.subtitle: Average annual dropout rate, %

explain.what: The share of students who leave school during the year at each stage, from UDISE+.
explain.read: Lower is better. Secondary-stage dropout is several times higher than primary, which is where most children are lost.
explain.why: Dropout shows whether rising enrolment turns into completed schooling; secondary dropout is the main focus of Samagra Shiksha.

mospi_school_dropout.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 74 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Number of Universities (AISHE)
meta.subtitle: Universities and university-level institutions

explain.what: The number of universities in India in each All India Survey on Higher Education.
explain.read: Each bar is an academic year; steady growth means new central, State, private and deemed universities opening.
explain.why: More institutions widen access, but the quality of what is taught matters as much as the count.

aishe_institutions.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 1 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Number of Colleges (AISHE)
meta.subtitle: Colleges affiliated to universities

explain.what: The number of colleges in India in each AISHE round.
explain.read: Bars rising year on year show expansion; most new colleges are private and small.
explain.why: Colleges teach the bulk of India's undergraduates, so their spread decides how many students can get a degree near home.

aishe_colleges.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 2 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Higher Education Enrolment by Sex (AISHE)
meta.subtitle: Estimated students enrolled

explain.what: The estimated number of students enrolled in higher education, split by sex.
explain.read: Women's enrolment has nearly caught up with men's; where the lines cross, women outnumber men.
explain.why: Higher-education enrolment builds the skilled workforce, and women's rising share is one of India's quieter social shifts.

aishe_enrolment_by_sex.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Higher Education Enrolment by Level (AISHE) (2021-22)
meta.subtitle: Share of students by programme level

explain.what: How students in higher education are spread across programme levels in the latest AISHE round.
explain.read: Undergraduates are the overwhelming majority; Ph.D. students are a sliver, which is relevant to India's research capacity.
explain.why: The mix shows whether the system mostly produces first degrees or advanced skills and research.

aishe_enrolment_by_level.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2021-22.

meta.title: Higher Education GER by Social Group (AISHE)
meta.subtitle: Gross enrolment ratio, age 18-23, %

explain.what: Higher-education enrolment as a share of the 18-23 age group for all students, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
explain.read: The gap between the 'All' line and the SC and ST lines measures unequal access; narrowing gaps mean more inclusive growth.
explain.why: GER is the headline access measure under NEP 2020 (target 50% by 2035), and group gaps guide scholarships and reservation policy.

aishe_ger_social_groups.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 6 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

meta.title: Higher Education GER by State (AISHE) (2021-22)
meta.subtitle: Gross enrolment ratio, age 18-23, %

explain.what: The higher-education gross enrolment ratio in each State and UT for the latest AISHE round.
explain.read: Longer bars mean more young people in college. Southern States and some UTs lead; large northern and eastern States trail.
explain.why: State gaps show where new colleges, scholarships and hostels would do the most to raise national enrolment.

meta.title: Malaria Cases (NCVBDC)
meta.subtitle: Reported cases nationwide

explain.what: Malaria cases reported through the National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control, with the more dangerous P. falciparum cases shown separately.
explain.read: Falling lines mean fewer infections; India's caseload has dropped by more than 80% since 2015.
explain.why: India aims to eliminate malaria by 2030, so steady declines, especially in falciparum cases, track progress toward that goal.

mospi_malaria_cases.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 119 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Values for 2023, 2024 are marked provisional by the source. National totals are the sum of State/UT reports; the most recent years are provisional.

meta.title: Dengue Cases (NCVBDC)
meta.subtitle: Reported cases nationwide

explain.what: Laboratory-reported dengue cases in India each year.
explain.read: Bars swing with monsoon conditions and urban mosquito breeding; the long-run trend is upward, partly because testing has improved.
explain.why: Dengue is an expanding urban health threat linked to water storage, construction and a warming climate, with no widely used vaccine yet.

mospi_dengue_cases.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 120 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Values for 2023 are marked provisional by the source. National totals are the sum of State/UT reports; the most recent years are provisional.

meta.title: Registered Motor Vehicles
meta.subtitle: Vehicles on record, transport vs non-transport (MoRTH)

explain.what: The total stock of registered motor vehicles, split into private (non-transport: two-wheelers and cars) and commercial (transport: buses, trucks, taxis).
explain.read: Bars show the fleet on record; private vehicles make up the overwhelming majority.
explain.why: Vehicle numbers drive fuel demand, urban congestion and air pollution, and set the scale of the EV transition.

meta.title: Trains Run Daily

explain.what: Average number of passenger and goods trains run each day.
explain.read: Passenger trains per day grew 5.2% and goods trains 12.9% between 2022-23 and 2023-24.
explain.why: Train counts show how intensively the track is used.

rail_passenger_suburban_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I, suburban journeys divided by total journeys; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

meta.title: Suburban Share of Journeys
meta.subtitle: Suburban journeys as a share of all passenger journeys

explain.what: Suburban passenger journeys divided by total passenger journeys for each year.
explain.read: Suburban journeys were 57.65% of the 2023-24 total.
explain.why: The share distinguishes commuter traffic from long-distance demand.

rail_passenger_non_suburban_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I, non-suburban journeys divided by total journeys; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

meta.title: Non-Suburban Share of Journeys
meta.subtitle: Non-suburban journeys as a share of all passenger journeys

explain.what: Non-suburban passenger journeys divided by total passenger journeys for each year.
explain.read: Non-suburban journeys were 42.35% of the 2023-24 total.
explain.why: This share tracks the long-distance portion of passenger traffic.

rail_passenger_average_lead_calculated.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Tables I and II; passenger-km divided by passengers originating; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

meta.title: Calculated Average Passenger Journey
meta.subtitle: Passenger-km divided by passenger journeys

explain.what: Average journey length calculated from passenger-kilometres and journeys originating.
explain.read: The ratio was 154.19 km per journey in 2023-24; it is calculated independently of the reported average lead.
explain.why: It cross-checks the relationship between passenger volume and distance travelled.

rail_passenger_km_index.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table II; passenger-kilometres indexed to 1950-51; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

meta.title: Passenger-Km Index
meta.subtitle: Passenger-kilometres indexed to 1950-51

explain.what: Passenger-kilometres as an index with 1950-51 set to 100.
explain.read: The index reached 1600.6 in 2023-24.
explain.why: The index shows long-run growth in passenger transport work.

rail_freight_tonnes.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I (revenue-earning freight, tonnes originating, excluding Konkan Railway); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Freight Originating
meta.subtitle: Revenue-earning tonnes loaded by Indian Railways

explain.what: Revenue-earning freight originating on Indian Railways, in million tonnes.
explain.read: From 73 million tonnes in 1950-51 to 1,588 million tonnes in 2023-24, about 21.7 times higher.
explain.why: Rail carries the bulk commodities (coal, ore, cement, foodgrains) that supply industry.

rail_freight_ntkm.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I (net tonne kilometres); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Freight Output (Net Tonne-Km)
meta.subtitle: Tonnes moved multiplied by distance

explain.what: Net tonne-kilometres: freight tonnage multiplied by distance moved.
explain.read: Output reached 973,968 million NTKM in 2023-24, about 26 times 1950-51.
explain.why: NTKM measures transport work; tonnes alone ignore haul length.

rail_freight_lead.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I (average lead of freight); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Average Freight Haul
meta.subtitle: Average lead of a tonne of freight

explain.what: Average distance a tonne of freight is carried.
explain.read: Average haul peaked at 754 km in 1980-81 and was 613 km in 2023-24.
explain.why: Haul length affects wagon use and freight earnings per tonne.

rail_freight_commodity_mix.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, commodity-wise loading 2023-24; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Freight by Commodity (2023-24)
meta.subtitle: Share of 1,588 million tonnes loaded

explain.what: Revenue-earning freight by commodity group in 2023-24.
explain.read: Coal is 49.55% of loading (thermal power houses alone 38.19%), then iron ore 11.39%, cement 9.62% and containers 5.34%.
explain.why: Rail freight depends heavily on bulk coal.

rail_freight_commodity_change.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, commodity-wise loading 2022-23 vs 2023-24; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Commodity Loading: 2022-23 vs 2023-24
meta.subtitle: Tonnes loaded by commodity group

explain.what: Tonnes carried for each commodity group in the last two years.
explain.read: Coal added 59.6 million tonnes and iron ore 20.8 million; foodgrains fell by 19.5 million.
explain.why: Year-on-year changes show which commodities drove growth.

rail_freight_loading_pib.note: Ministry of Railways via PIB: originating freight loading was 1,233 MT in 2020-21 (Lok Sabha reply, PIB release 2201815), 1,590.68 MT in 2023-24 and 1,617.38 MT in 2024-25, up 1.68% (PIB release 2117417, 1 April 2025, opening freight-loading paragraph). These cover all originating loading, so they differ slightly from the Year Book's revenue-earning series.

meta.title: Freight Loading to 2024-25
meta.subtitle: Originating loading, latest Ministry figures

explain.what: Total originating freight loading, from Ministry of Railways statements.
explain.read: Loading reached 1,617.38 million tonnes in 2024-25; the Ministry says this makes Indian Railways the second-largest freight carrier in the world.
explain.why: It extends the series past the Year Book's 2023-24 end year.

rail_freight_commodity_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation commodity table, 2023-24 loading as a share of the 1,588.06 million tonnes reported in Table I; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Commodity Shares of Loading
meta.subtitle: Commodity tonnes as a share of 2023-24 revenue-earning loading

explain.what: Each commodity group's reported loading divided by total revenue-earning tonnes originating.
explain.read: Coal accounted for 49.55% of 2023-24 revenue-earning loading.
explain.why: The shares show the commodity concentration of rail freight.

rail_freight_commodity_growth_pct.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation commodity-wise loading table, 2022-23 to 2023-24; percentage changes calculated from table values; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Commodity Loading Growth
meta.subtitle: Percent change in tonnes loaded by commodity

explain.what: Year-on-year percentage change in commodity loading between 2022-23 and 2023-24.
explain.read: Coal loading rose 8.20%; foodgrains changed by -27.47%.
explain.why: Growth by commodity identifies which goods gained or lost loading.

rail_freight_average_haul_calculated.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I; net tonne-kilometres divided by revenue-earning tonnes; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Calculated Average Freight Haul
meta.subtitle: Net tonne-km divided by originating tonnes

explain.what: Average freight haul calculated by dividing net tonne-kilometres by tonnes originating.
explain.read: The calculated average haul was 613.31 km in 2023-24.
explain.why: The quotient ties freight volume to the distance moved.

rail_freight_loading_benchmark_change.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I; change between adjacent listed originating-tonnage benchmarks; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

meta.title: Freight Loading Change Between Benchmarks
meta.subtitle: Change in originating tonnes since the prior listed year

explain.what: Difference in revenue-earning tonnes originating between adjacent listed benchmark years.
explain.read: Loading increased by 78.96 million tonnes between 2022-23 and 2023-24.
explain.why: The changes reveal the varying scale of long-run growth.

rail_locomotive_mix.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, locomotives on 31 March 2024; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Locomotives by Traction (2023-24)
meta.subtitle: 15,110 locomotives by type

explain.what: Locomotive fleet by traction type on 31 March 2024.
explain.read: Electric locomotives are 70.7% of the fleet; 38 steam locomotives remain.
explain.why: Fleet mix follows the electrification of the route.

rail_locomotive_change.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, number of locomotives (2022-23 revised); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Locomotive Fleet: 2022-23 vs 2023-24
meta.subtitle: Locomotives by traction type

explain.what: Number of electric, diesel and steam locomotives in the last two years.
explain.read: Electric locomotives grew by 1,110 while diesel fell by 333.
explain.why: Shows the shift from diesel to electric traction year by year.

rail_coach_fleet.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, number of coaches (2022-23 revised); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Coach Fleet: 2022-23 vs 2023-24
meta.subtitle: Passenger and other coaching vehicles

explain.what: Coaches by type; the total was 91,948 in 2023-24 including rail cars.
explain.read: Other coaching vehicles grew fastest, by 14%; passenger carriages grew 0.5%.
explain.why: Coach numbers limit how many passengers can be carried.

rail_wagon_fleet.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, number of wagons (2022-23 revised); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Wagon Fleet
meta.subtitle: Freight wagons owned by Indian Railways

explain.what: Total wagons owned by Indian Railways.
explain.read: The fleet grew by 12,888 wagons (4.1%) to 327,991.
explain.why: Wagon availability caps freight loading.

rail_wagon_turnround.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, Wagon Utilisation (broad gauge); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Wagon Turn-Round Time
meta.subtitle: Days for a wagon to complete a loading cycle

explain.what: Average days for a broad-gauge wagon to complete one loading cycle.
explain.read: Turn-round lengthened from 4.70 to 5.11 days.
explain.why: A shorter turn-round lets the same fleet carry more freight.

rail_goods_load.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, goods train utilisation (broad gauge, all traction). Average goods-train speed fell from 30.8 to 25.0 km/h over the same year; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Average Goods Train Load
meta.subtitle: Net and gross load per goods train

explain.what: Average net and gross load of a broad-gauge goods train.
explain.read: Net load per train rose 9.3% to 1,899 tonnes, while average goods-train speed fell to 25.0 km/h.
explain.why: Heavier trains move more per path, but slower speeds lengthen transit times.

rail_locomotive_traction_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, locomotive counts by traction on 31 March 2023 and 31 March 2024; shares calculated from category totals; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Locomotive Fleet by Traction Share
meta.subtitle: Electric, diesel and steam shares

explain.what: Locomotive counts by traction as a share of all reported electric, diesel and steam locomotives.
explain.read: Electric locomotives were 70.65% of the listed fleet in 2023-24.
explain.why: Shares make the traction transition comparable despite fleet growth.

rail_coach_category_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, number of coaches by category, 2022-23 revised and 2023-24; shares calculated over the three listed categories; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Share of Listed Coach Categories
meta.subtitle: Composition of the three reported coach groups

explain.what: Share of passenger carriages, other coaching vehicles and EMU/MEMU coaches among those listed categories.
explain.read: Passenger carriages were 72.53% of the listed 2023-24 categories.
explain.why: Category shares show how the reported coaching fleet is composed.

rail_daily_goods_train_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, daily passenger and goods trains run; goods share calculated from the two reported totals; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Goods Trains as Share of Daily Trains
meta.subtitle: Goods trains among reported passenger and goods trains

explain.what: Goods trains run daily divided by the combined daily passenger and goods train counts.
explain.read: Goods trains made up 47.04% of the two reported train groups in 2023-24.
explain.why: The mix compares passenger and freight operating intensity.

rail_goods_load_utilisation_pct.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, average net and gross goods-train loads; net-to-gross ratios calculated from the reported values; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

meta.title: Average Net Load as Share of Gross Load
meta.subtitle: Net tonnes per goods train relative to gross tonnes

explain.what: Average net goods-train load divided by average gross load.
explain.read: The net-to-gross ratio was 61.56% in 2023-24.
explain.why: The ratio shows the share of average gross train weight represented by payload.

rail_accidents_by_type.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, consequential train accidents by type, including Konkan Railway; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Consequential Train Accidents by Type
meta.subtitle: Accidents per year, 2019-20 to 2023-24

explain.what: Consequential train accidents split into derailments, collisions, fires, level-crossing and other accidents.
explain.read: Derailments are the largest category (25 of 40 in 2023-24); fire accidents rose to 9.
explain.why: Type-wise counts show where safety work matters most.

rail_accidents_total.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, total consequential train accidents including Konkan Railway; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Total Consequential Train Accidents
meta.subtitle: Accidents per year

explain.what: Total consequential train accidents.
explain.why: Raw counts show how many serious incidents occurred.

rail_accident_rate.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, accidents per million train kilometres, the Year Book's principal safety index; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Accidents per Million Train-Km
meta.subtitle: Accident rate normalised for traffic

explain.what: Consequential accidents divided by million train-kilometres run.
explain.read: The rate has held at 0.03 since 2020-21, against 0.05 in 2019-20.
explain.why: A rate shows safety per unit of traffic, unlike a raw count.

rail_accident_mix.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, 2023-24: 40 consequential accidents; none at level crossings or miscellaneous; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Accident Types (2023-24)
meta.subtitle: Composition of 40 consequential accidents

explain.what: Share of each accident type among the 40 consequential accidents in 2023-24.
explain.read: Derailments are 62.5%, fires 22.5% and collisions 15%.
explain.why: Shows which accident types dominate.

rail_derailment_collision_trend.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, consequential train accidents table; derailments plus collisions calculated from the listed types; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Derailments and Collisions
meta.subtitle: Combined derailment and collision counts

explain.what: Yearly derailment and collision counts added together from the consequential-accident table.
explain.read: There were 31 derailments and collisions in 2023-24.
explain.why: These two accident types together account for a large share of consequential incidents.

rail_derailment_share_pct.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, consequential train accidents table; derailments divided by each year's total; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Derailments as Share of Consequential Accidents
meta.subtitle: Derailments divided by all listed consequential accidents

explain.what: Derailments as a percentage of all consequential train accidents listed for each year.
explain.read: Derailments accounted for 62.50% of consequential accidents in 2023-24.
explain.why: The share distinguishes the leading accident type from the overall count.

rail_accident_yoy_change_pct.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Safety, consequential train accidents table; year-on-year changes calculated from the sum of listed accident types; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 52-59.

meta.title: Year-on-Year Accident Count Change
meta.subtitle: Percent change in consequential accident totals

explain.what: Year-on-year percentage change in the sum of the five reported accident categories.
explain.read: The total changed by -16.67% between 2022-23 and 2023-24.
explain.why: Year-on-year change shows direction as well as scale.

rail_revenue_expenses.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Key Statistics, financial results; Year Book 2023-24, p. 3.

meta.title: Railway Revenue and Expenses
meta.subtitle: Rs crore, 2022-23 and 2023-24

explain.what: Total revenue, expenses and net revenue of Indian Railways.
explain.read: Revenue rose 6.4% to Rs 2.55 lakh crore; expenses rose 6.5%, leaving Rs 3,260 crore of net revenue.
explain.why: Net revenue is small relative to turnover.

rail_earnings.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business and Freight Operation, earnings (freight excludes demurrage and wharfage); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-45.

meta.title: Passenger vs Freight Earnings
meta.subtitle: Earnings by business, Rs crore

explain.what: Earnings from passenger and freight services.
explain.read: Passenger earnings grew 11.5% and freight 3.6%; freight is 70% of the two combined.
explain.why: Freight is the larger earner.

rail_financial_ratios.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Some Selected Financial Ratio; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 7-8.

meta.title: Operating and Working Ratios
meta.subtitle: Expenses as a percentage of earnings

explain.what: Operating ratio is expenditure as a share of earnings; lower is better.
explain.read: The overall ratio was 98.43%. Goods runs at 67.55% while coaching is 177.69%, meaning Rs 1.78 is spent for every Re 1 earned from passengers.
explain.why: The ratio shows how much of each rupee earned is left for investment.

rail_yield.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Some Selected Financial Ratio, earning/yield ratios based on apportioned earning; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 7-8.

meta.title: Passenger and Freight Yield
meta.subtitle: Average revenue per unit of traffic

explain.what: Average revenue per passenger-km and per net tonne-km.
explain.read: Passenger yield was 66.40 paise per passenger-km and freight 170.31 paise per net tonne-km.
explain.why: Yield compares what the railway earns on each unit of traffic.

rail_earnings_mix_share.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business and Freight Operation earnings table; shares calculated over those two earning streams; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-45.

meta.title: Passenger and Freight Earnings Shares
meta.subtitle: Share of combined passenger and freight earnings

explain.what: Passenger and freight earnings as percentages of the two categories' combined earnings.
explain.read: Freight represented 70.12% of combined passenger and freight earnings in 2023-24.
explain.why: The shares show the relative contribution of the two main traffic earnings streams.

rail_net_revenue_margin_pct.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Key Statistics, financial results; net revenue divided by total revenue; Year Book 2023-24, p. 3.

meta.title: Net Revenue Margin
meta.subtitle: Net revenue as a share of total revenue

explain.what: Reported net revenue divided by total railway revenue for each year.
explain.read: Net revenue was 1.28% of total revenue in 2023-24.
explain.why: The margin shows the net result relative to the scale of railway earnings.

rail_financial_growth_rates.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Key Statistics, financial results; growth rates calculated from reported total revenue and expenses; Year Book 2023-24, p. 3.

meta.title: Revenue and Expense Growth
meta.subtitle: Year-on-year change in railway revenue and expenses

explain.what: Percentage change in reported total revenue and total expenses from 2022-23 to 2023-24.
explain.read: Revenue increased 6.37%; expenses increased 6.47%.
explain.why: Comparing the two growth rates shows whether expenses grew faster than revenue.

meta.subtitle: Goods transported by railway

rail_wb_passenger_trend.note: World Bank indicator IS.RRS.PASG.KM, compiled from national railway data (UIC / ITF). Gaps are years a country did not report.

meta.title: Rail Passengers: India vs Peers
meta.subtitle: Passenger-kilometres carried by railway

explain.read: India is the orange line; compare its trajectory with each peer.

meta.title: Share of Rail Passenger-Km Among Peers (2019)
meta.subtitle: Peer share of rail passenger-km

explain.what: Each country's share of the peer group's rail passenger-km.
explain.read: India ranks 2 of 10 countries in this comparison.

rail_wb_route_rank.note: World Bank indicator IS.RRS.TOTL.KM, 2019 (latest year most compared countries report). India ranks 4 of 7 countries shown.

dg_elections_effective_candidates_2022_s.source: Election Commission of India candidate results (data/recent-indian-elections.json)
dg_elections_effective_candidates_2022_s.note: For each state/UT in the 2022 State Assembly results, calculates the effective number of candidates in each seat as 1 / sum(candidate vote-share squared), then averages those seat values. NOTA and seats without at least two candidates with reported votes are excluded. This competition measure is distinct from raw candidate counts in the existing election indices.

meta.title: 2022 State Assembly: Effective Candidates per Seat by State
meta.subtitle: Mean constituency effective number of candidates

explain.what: Mean constituency-level effective number of candidates for each state/UT.
explain.read: A seat's value is 1 divided by the sum of squared candidate vote shares; larger values indicate votes are spread across more candidates.
explain.why: Complements raw candidate-count charts with a vote-weighted measure of electoral competition.
